compiled_state.title: Calibration program observability: rollup metrics, trend tracking, bug-detection-channel attribution, and program-level health reporting
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

The six calibration-program epics (a03c-d55e Closure Checks; 94ed-f55c plan-time intent allocation; d566-afa6 Tier 1+2 gen-time prevention; 7f42-e41f suite growth metrics; 69e8-af39 bug/review feedback loop; 411b-a047 mutation infrastructure Tier 3; 4911-c7ba bug-type taxonomy) produce per-event measurement signals — reviewer findings, intent coverage, mutation kill rates, negative-example extractions, graduation telemetry — but no aggregation layer. The headline program-success question — "what fraction of bugs are caught by tests vs review vs production, and is the ratio improving?" — is unanswerable today because bug tickets carry no detection-channel attribution and per-event data is never rolled up. The maintainer (sole stakeholder for the test-writing system in this repo) needs a measurement substrate to evaluate whether the system is improving over time. Without this epic, the six calibration epics ship infrastructure that delivers value but the maintainer cannot tell if it's working; the cost of the gap is silent regression — the system could degrade without anyone noticing.

This epic ships in two milestones back-to-back. Milestone 1 adds a detected_by:<channel> tag to bug tickets with seven allowed values (tests, review-llm, review-human, production, user-report, internal-dogfood, other); required for CLI_user-tagged bugs via the create-bug dialogue; auto-set via infer-detected-by.sh for the three agent filing paths (411b mutation auto-bug, /dso:fix-bug Phase G, debug-everything) based on filing context, defaulting to other when context is insufficient. No backfill — closed bugs remain other; time-series starts from M1 ship date. Milestone 2 builds the rollup tooling: a single plugins/dso/scripts/calibration-report.sh with subcommands (monthly, quarterly, mutation-append, churn-append, query <sub>); a thin /dso:test-quality-report skill wraps it for manual invocation; .github/workflows/calibration-rollup.yml runs per-PR mutation-append + churn-append and cron monthly + quarterly; rollup comments are posted via the ticket CLI to three tracking tickets (calibration-program-health, mutation-history, suite-churn-history). Hybrid data sourcing: mutation findings and suite-churn pre-aggregated per-PR; bug counts and reviewer-finding rates queried on demand. Rule-effectiveness measurement folds into the monthly rollup using promoted-to-standard:* tags + detected_by + bug-type-<slug> from 4911-c7ba.

Tickets-as-storage pattern throughout — rollups accumulate as comments on dedicated tracking tickets so they remain searchable via the ticket CLI, consistent with the rest of the calibration program's storage choices.

## Success Criteria

1. (M1) Bug tickets carry a detected_by:<channel> tag from the seven allowed values (tests, review-llm, review-human, production, user-report, internal-dogfood, other); create-bug dialogue prompts the human filer when the bug is CLI_user-tagged; infer-detected-by.sh sets the value from filing context for 411b mutation auto-bug, /dso:fix-bug Phase G, and debug-everything paths, defaulting to other when context is insufficient. Verified by unit tests covering each helper branch and an integration test for the CLI_user dialogue path. The helper is committed with the executable bit set and includes a self-test guard that fails CI if the binary is non-executable.

2. (M1) plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/bug-report-template.md and plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/SKILL.md document the detected_by field and its allowed values; .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --has-tag=detected_by:tests returns only bug-type tickets filed at or after M1 ship date (non-bug tickets that accidentally carry the tag do not appear in the result).

3. (M2) plugins/dso/scripts/calibration-report.sh supports subcommands monthly, quarterly, mutation-append, churn-append, and query <sub> (with sub values: intents-with-low-kill-rate, intents-without-coverage, bugs-by-channel-and-type, rule-effectiveness <rule-id>); each subcommand produces output matching its documented schema for a dry-run input fixture; the script is idempotent on repeated invocation for the same period (does not post duplicate comments).

4. (M2) Given a synthetic ticket fixture with a known detected_by distribution (e.g., 3 detected_by:tests, 2 detected_by:review-llm, 1 detected_by:production, 2 detected_by:other), calibration-report.sh monthly returns channel counts that exactly match the fixture. This fixture-driven correctness test runs in CI via calibration-rollup.yml before any append step and is also invoked as part of the M2 release gate locally.

5. (M2) /dso:test-quality-report skill is registered, invokes calibration-report.sh, and surfaces monthly and quarterly rollup outputs for manual invocation.

6. (M2) .github/workflows/calibration-rollup.yml runs mutation-append and churn-append on PR-merge events (with a per-PR append safeguard — advisory lock on the tracking ticket or post-append verification — so concurrent fast-follow PR merges produce neither duplicates nor lost entries) and runs monthly + quarterly on cron triggers using a single declared timezone (UTC) that the aggregation logic also uses for bucket boundaries; CI dry-run posts the expected comment shape to a test ticket; the workflow surfaces a non-zero exit and CI failure (not a silent skip) when calibration-report.sh fails or when a target tracking ticket is missing.

7. **SC7 (self-use, Probe-1 remediation, architecture-vs-evidence audit 2026-05-16):** Bugs filed during the a34c sprint exercise the calibration-channel attribution end-to-end before sprint close. At least one bug filed during the a34c sprint (via `/dso:create-bug`, sub-agent, or debug path) carries a valid `detected_by:<channel>` tag from the seven allowed values, AND `calibration-report.sh monthly` (run against a synthetic fixture or the in-flight ticket set) returns a non-empty channel breakdown that includes the just-filed bug's channel.

   Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
   - `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --type=bug --format=llm | python3 -c "import json,sys; ts=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sum(1 for t in ts for tag in (t.get('tags') or []) if tag.startswith('detected_by:')))"` returns ≥1.
   - `plugins/dso/scripts/calibration-report.sh monthly --fixture=tests/fixtures/a34c-sprint-bugs` returns exit 0 with a `bugs-by-channel` section containing ≥1 entry.
## Scenario Analysis

Surviving scenarios after Red/Blue Team filter — these are design constraints for preplanning task decomposition, not separate SCs.

Detected_by field integrity:
- CLI_user bug filed without detected_by prompt produces silent schema gap (high) — needs CLI-level enforcement, not just SKILL.md guidance.
- infer-detected-by.sh ambiguous-context path silently mis-tags when filing context is misleading (high) — e.g., human runs /dso:fix-bug on a production bug; filing context looks like review-llm.
- Duplicate detected_by tags on same ticket produce double-counting (medium) — calibration-report.sh must deduplicate.
- detected_by tag applied to non-bug tickets contaminates channel query (medium) — queries must filter by ticket type.

Tracking ticket comment accumulation:
- Comment thread exceeds ticket CLI performance threshold at year 2+ (high) — known SIGURG scaling pattern (bug 2f20-eb16) not yet evaluated for single-ticket comment depth.
- calibration-report.sh scans full comment history rather than using a cursor (high) — linear query cost growth.
- No compaction or archival strategy (medium) — comments are permanent; mutation-history grows indefinitely.

Pre-aggregated stream concurrency:
- mutation-append races with fast-follow PR merges (critical) — ticket CLI append not described as atomic across concurrent writers.
- Skipped or failed mutation-append leaves invisible gap (critical) — no retry/alerting; unrecoverable past GHA's 90-day retention.
- On-demand reviewer-findings query reads tickets-branch at stale ref (high) — GHA cached workspace may miss recent findings.

CI cron workflow:
- Month-boundary cron in UTC misaligns with bug-timestamp local time (high) — unify timezone across cron and aggregation.
- Double-run on cron + manual workflow_dispatch produces duplicate comment (medium) — needs idempotency check.
- GHA cron skipped run leaves permanent gap with no alerting (high) — trend queries silently bridge missing periods.

Configuration and deployment:
- Three tracking tickets must pre-exist before first CI run (high) — needs bootstrap/create-if-missing guard.
- calibration-rollup.yml referencing absent calibration-report.sh on PR merges (high) — workflow must guard for script existence or M1/M2 ship-order must enforce co-arrival.
- infer-detected-by.sh non-executable causes silent fallthrough to 'other' (high) — CLAUDE.md rule 11 + the self-test guard in SC1 mitigates.

## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)

### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detected_by:<channel>` tag (7 allowed values) | SC1: `/dso:create-bug` dialogue when CLI_user-tagged; `infer-detected-by.sh` for 411b auto-bug + Phase G + debug-everything paths; default `:other` | Stable (no mutation) | SC3 calibration-report.sh aggregation; downstream 69e8 / 411b / 4911 consumers | Implicit with bug ticket lifecycle; persists on closed tickets as historical attribution record |
| Tracking ticket `calibration-program-health` | Bootstrap guard per SC6 (workflow fails CI if missing); created once at epic ship | SC3 monthly/quarterly append subcommands | calibration-report.sh queries; manual review via /dso:test-quality-report | N/A — persistent by design. Comment thread is intentional append-only historical record per event-sourced ticket-system v3 semantics. Converts the audit's "no compaction" gap into a documented design choice. |
| Tracking ticket `mutation-history` | Same as `calibration-program-health` | SC6 mutation-append on PR-merge | calibration-report.sh `query intents-with-low-kill-rate` | Same as `calibration-program-health` |
| Tracking ticket `suite-churn-history` | Same | SC6 churn-append on PR-merge | calibration-report.sh `query rule-effectiveness` | Same |
| Per-PR append safeguard (advisory lock or post-append verification) | Per SC6 — chosen mechanism declared in calibration-rollup.yml | Each PR-merge run acquires/releases | The append job itself | Implicit per workflow run; lock is short-lived, released by workflow exit |

Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket exists calibration-program-health && .claude/scripts/dso ticket exists mutation-history && .claude/scripts/dso ticket exists suite-churn-history` returns 0.
- `grep -n 'advisory.*lock\|post-append verification' plugins/dso/workflows/calibration-rollup.yml` confirms the chosen safeguard is declared.

Closes the audit's named gap: tracking-ticket RETIRE = "N/A — persistent by design" (append-only historical record per ticket-system v3 semantics).
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The original 2026-05-16 pass deferred probe 6. The session-completability rule treats gh CLI + ticket-CLI as in-session-verifiable. Adding the structured block:

| Resource | In-session verification command | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Three tracking tickets exist | `.claude/scripts/dso ticket exists calibration-program-health && .claude/scripts/dso ticket exists mutation-history && .claude/scripts/dso ticket exists suite-churn-history` | Returns 0 (all three present) |
| calibration-rollup.yml is active | `gh workflow list --json name,state \| jq '[.[] \| select(.name == "calibration-rollup") \| select(.state == "active")] \| length'` | ≥1 |
| Cron expression is valid + scheduled | `gh workflow view calibration-rollup.yml --yaml \| grep -E '^\s+- cron:'` | Returns ≥1 cron line; expression parses (no GHA validation error in `gh workflow view`) |
| Recent run succeeded (cron reliability indicator) | `gh run list --workflow=calibration-rollup.yml --limit=10 --json conclusion --jq '[.[] \| select(.conclusion == "success")] \| length'` | ≥1 in the last 10 runs; if zero, sprint surfaces the gap and operator decides (force-trigger or defer epic close) |
| Branch protection includes calibration check | `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/branches/main/protection 2>/dev/null \| jq '.required_status_checks.contexts // [] \| length'` | ≥0 — branch protection is OPTIONAL; documented posture either way |
| Workflow surfaces non-zero exit when tracking ticket missing (SC6) | Synthetic test: rename one tracking ticket via `dso ticket edit --title=...test-rename`, trigger workflow, assert run conclusion != success; restore name; verify rerun succeeds | Test pass before sprint close |

Converts the audit's prose-only external dependencies (GHA cron + tracking-ticket bootstrap + branch protection) into structured in-session checks. Cron-skipped-run-without-alerting remains a residual operational risk; the "recent run succeeded in last 10" check surfaces it before sprint closure rather than deferring entirely.
## Dependencies

Soft consumers (this epic consumes their outputs; no hard blocking for design):
- a03c-d55e — closure-checks-aware verifier findings
- 94ed-f55c — intent allocation manifest
- d566-afa6 — Tier 1/Tier 2 reviewer findings
- 7f42-e41f — intent-coverage findings
- 69e8-af39 — retro graduation telemetry; consumes detected_by as candidate-weighting signal from this epic
- 411b-a047 — per-PR mutation kill rates; auto-files mutation-breach bugs (will set detected_by:tests once this epic ships)
- 4911-c7ba — bug-type-<slug> taxonomy joined with detected_by:<channel> for cross-classification reporting

Sequencing notes:
- M2 core script + skill is independently mergeable before the GHA workflow; the workflow ships as a follow-on task within the same milestone to reduce blast radius on CI iteration.
- M1 must merge before the 411b auto-bug pathway is activated; coordinate with 411b implementation to add detected_by:tests to infer-detected-by.sh output prior to 411b going live (coordination comment already on 411b-a047).
- M1 ship triggers a notification to 69e8-af39 so its graduation candidate-weighting can begin using detected_by; 69e8 must not hardcode a fallback that silently ignores the tag.

## Out of Scope

- Test-caught-regression event tagging from CI logs (Gap G) — deferred P3+ follow-on per user direction.
- Custom dashboards / web UI — surface is ticket comments + script output.
- Real-time streaming metrics — periodic rollups only.
- Backfill of detected_by on closed bugs — time-series starts from M1 ship date.
- Operational meta-criterion (e.g., "first non-degenerate rollup posted") — relying on per-deliverable SCs.

## Coordination history (from prior session)

- Ticket comments on 411b-a047-18de-4516: its auto-bug-creation logic should set detected_by:tests when this epic ships.
- Ticket comments on 69e8-af39-7886-4ee9: its graduation phase can use detected_by as a candidate-weighting signal once this epic ships.
- Ticket comments on 4911-c7ba (via the now-closed cf65-e3b4-0bea-4756 story): detection-CHANNEL is a separate dimension from 4911's bug-TYPE taxonomy.
- cf65-e3b4-0bea-4756 closure comment recorded the re-parenting rationale.

## Brainstorm session decisions (2026-05-12)

Approach chosen: Option A — single shell script with thin skill wrapper, ticket-CLI-native.

Open-question resolutions:
1. Phased delivery: M1 detected_by first, M2 rollup back-to-back.
2. Rollup cadence: scheduled monthly + quarterly via GHA cron.
3. detected_by enforcement: required for CLI_user-tagged bugs; agent-filed bugs auto-set via infer-detected-by.sh based on filing context, default 'other'.
4. Backfill: none; closed bugs remain 'other'.
5. Tracking tickets: three (calibration-program-health, mutation-history, suite-churn-history); no yearly partitioning.
6. Aggregation timing: hybrid — pre-aggregate mutation+churn per-PR; query bugs+reviews on demand.
7. Meta-criterion: skipped; per-deliverable SCs suffice (with the fixture-driven correctness SC added during fidelity review).

comments.body: Research note (session 2026-05-17, see docs/findings/code-review-fp-research-2026-05-17.md): The published consensus on FP-reduction-system metrics differs from precision/recall/F1 in ways that affect this epic's M2 query schema. (1) Balanced Accuracy (Youden's J statistic; arXiv 2512.08121) is prevalence-independent and recommended over F1 for tuning judge/verifier systems where class prevalence shifts over time. (2) FPR_P and FPR_R (false-positive-reduction precision/recall — arXiv 2601.18844 Datadog industrial deployment) measure precision and recall *for the FP class itself*, which is the right denominator when the goal is reducing FPs rather than maximizing finding recall. Recommendation: add Balanced Accuracy and FPR_P/FPR_R to the 'query rule-effectiveness <rule-id>' subcommand output (SC3) alongside any conventional metrics. Cost: small math additions to calibration-report.sh; large analytical payoff for downstream rule pruning.
